output.reason: The cited bullet [ev-8c0cecc71daf] links to the `service_name` label section, and that section is shown in the context [ev-b07a4021f30c]. It says that by default Loki 3.0 assigns a `service_name` label to all ingested logs. It looks for source labels in a fixed order [ev-92063a2a5bac, ev-2690c7915f58, ev-61d6d2b50a95, ev-c8bbef5b1d06, ev-d0c9247a44d4, ev-33c9df8cd833, ev-ba4422942cd3, ev-6c97458131e0, ev-73d501ad9fa3, ev-7e86af7082a3, ev-ea984d665a12] and uses `unknown_service` when none of them match. The same section covers who is exposed and what happens if the operator does nothing: anyone ingesting logs without already using a `service_name` label (the doc calls it `service_label`) gets the new label added automatically. The lookup list can be changed through `discover_service_name` in `limits_config`, and an empty value turns the feature off.
